# R000C independent recording decision — reconciled boundary

The fourth pilot did not establish a readable recording mode. The existing headless original-wrapper path nevertheless supplies the required C15 bounded acquisition-state pixels. These are different claims. All failed initial continuous watches remain failed.

This note supplements, and does not replace, `recording-decision.md`. The original recommendation to stop further recording-mode changes was a bounded diagnostic recommendation, not new owner authority and not a reason to halt independently executable C15 cases. The exact owner order was independently read and hashed: `../authority/owner-order.txt`, SHA256 `49e7d5809b5051e246eeac1841fc38b005de6122d6933faac36e080cc06e568d`. It authorizes bounded fixture work and the unchanged remaining matrix, reserves exact-head merge approval, and prohibits desktop interaction. The private owner order is not a proposed public artifact.

## Fourth pilot

`../native/firefox-single-headed-pilot/R000C-invalid-precip/` used the already pinned single-document preparse adapter, headed Firefox, video-only recording, and unchanged case/assertions/readiness/watch. The original video SHA256 is `5eb8e39258bca6c66e91adaa7b24569d2def6acf46d20efd0241e63625ee0765`. I independently decoded all 296 frames, verified every RGB digest and PTS against the original index, and inspected the native last frame (`firefox-single-headed-pilot/R000C-invalid-precip/last-original.png`). It is blank across the widget. All 296 frames at PTS 0–11.80 seconds are low-information candidates. The semantic assertions still pass, which cannot qualify unreadable pixels. The original continuous watch and state pixels are rejected; the source/fixture/browser identities and whole video remain retained.

The four-pilot comparison does not establish a source, renderer, capturer, document replacement, or encoder cause. Headed mode being readable in the exact prior R0007 control did not transfer to this R000C input. The two headed R000C pilots are all-blank; the two headless pilots contain both blank and complete original frames. This is contrary evidence that must remain visible, not a causal diagnosis. No further recording mode was recommended on these facts.

## C15 bounded state result

The immutable A02/C15 assertion requires actual request/native JSON consumption, admitted/cache values, header/effect state and relevant pixels. It does not impose a first-navigation-frame completion deadline. Running the five previously unexecuted canonical day inputs through the unchanged original-wrapper/headless path was therefore justified. It neither repeats the failed invalid-amount watch nor changes its predicate.

`firefox-day-readback-check.json` records independent raw reconciliation of all six cases, including the original `firefox-day/R000C-invalid-precip` acquisition. Canonical input equality, current source pins, actual Firefox executable identity, request target/zone/unit, native `Response.json()` reads, admitted/cache values, header text, raw model condition, precipitation permission/particles, independent lightning prohibition, no direct-observation claim, 325×530 geometry and footer bounds all agree. All 1,796 original frames and their PTS independently match the indexes.

I directly extracted and viewed the six native final frames under `firefox-day-remaining/` and `firefox-day/` beside this report. Null and absent temperature leave the temperature slot empty; true zero shows `0°`; healthy temperature shows `20°`. Null temperature alone still permits the quantity-supported model rain. Malformed and numerical-zero amounts show no rain, while 2 mm shows rain. The thunder condition icon remains present in every case, consistent with H5/H8. The header, buckle separation, six prayer rows and footer remain readable in these bounded states. This supports C15; it does not certify a continuous initial interval.

The candidate counts are diagnostic aids. They are not the visual acceptance oracle. The original failed pixels are preserved alongside the complete state crops, and no cutoff derived from the last bad frame becomes a new readiness or watch boundary.

## Separate C16 work

The unmodified driver already declared a 30-second initial night watch and a separate 30-second watch after ordinary healthy recovery before any Firefox acquisition. The three previously unexecuted original night inputs may independently test malformed-state pixels, actual recovery, Moon/layout preservation and real-clock default/reduced/full motion. A readable recovered interval can support that separately declared interval; it cannot rescue an unreadable initial interval. Any missing pixels inside the recovered interval would remain a failure even if later images were complete.

At this addendum's cut, the night matrix and indexes are not yet fully available for independent review. No C16 Firefox result, exact-head qualification, delivery or closure is granted here. Required remaining evidence is the original completed three night receipts/videos/indexes and actual pixel inspection of their predeclared intervals. An unassisted first-Moon presentation claim is also outside this evidence: the existing `qaState()` call can cause the lunar surface/state getter to adopt a pending preview. It does not install weather state, and the observer caveat is explicitly retained in `fixture-adaptation.json`.

All work for this addendum was offline and read-only except derived media and reports within `independent-review/`. The independent evidence scripts are `review_frontier.py` and `verify_firefox_completion.py`; neither launches a browser or changes the repository.
